title: Stellar Sweet Shop
caption: The star cluster NGC 2203, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble presents the star cluster NGC 2203 in the sharpest view yet obtained of it. Beyond its good looks, the cluster holds plenty of treats that have helped astronomers piece together how stars live.

Most of a star's life is spent on what astronomers call the main sequence, the long, steady stage when it burns fuel at an even pace. The Sun is a main-sequence star. In approximately 6 billion years its fuel will run out, and it will move on to its next stage and become a red giant.

NGC 2203 contains stars roughly twice as massive as the Sun. Astronomers studying them found that rotation might help explain why some of these stars linger longer than usual in the main-sequence phase.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 imaged the cluster through ultraviolet, blue-green and near-infrared filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, so part of this picture records light we could never see directly.
